questions.q: According to the Dalai Lama, what does basic spirituality mean?
a: Showing compassion, kindness and care for the people around you
Following the rituals of the religion you were born into
Meditating for several hours every single day
Believing in a creator who rewards good behavior
questions.why: Lesson 1 says basic spirituality is about compassion and caring, not about belonging to any religion.

questions.q: What mistake does the Dalai Lama say Westerners make about suffering?
a: Treating it as unnatural and therefore resisting it
Believing that only other people can truly suffer
Trying to fix it instead of simply accepting it
Talking about it too openly with friends
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Westerners think suffering is unnatural, and rejecting it turns them into victims.

questions.q: According to the summary, what is the root cause of suffering?
a: Resistance to change
A lack of close friendships
Unrealistic career ambitions
Not having enough money
questions.why: Lesson 2 states plainly that resisting change is the root cause of suffering.

questions.q: How does the Dalai Lama suggest building confidence?
a: From the inside, by being honest about what you can and cannot do
From the outside, by collecting praise and achievements
By comparing yourself with people who struggle more
By taking on challenges far beyond your current level
questions.why: Lesson 3 contrasts outer confidence with inner honesty about your limits.

questions.q: What two lessons did the author take from his uncle's early death?
a: Stop doing work you hate and spend more time with loved ones
Work harder while you can and save more money
Avoid thinking about death and stay busy
Travel more often and take fewer risks
questions.why: The review lists these two conclusions: quit work you dislike and value the time you have with family and friends.
